assertions.text: The flake provides three packages: the Antigravity 2.0 Base App (default), the Antigravity IDE, and the `agy` CLI, with GUI binaries wrapped in an FHS environment.
Repository development practice: hashes in `artifacts/versions.json` must be real SRI hashes obtained via `nix-prefetch-url` and `nix hash to-sri`; placeholder hashes fail CI before reaching users.
A daily GitHub Actions workflow (07:00 UTC) checks Google Cloud Run endpoints for new versions, verifies hashes, builds, and opens auto-merge PRs; release and branch-cleanup workflows follow.

Repository development practice: contributors fork, create a feature branch, test with `nix build` and `nix flake check`, and submit a PR; CLAUDE.md adds build, version-update, and workflow-testing checklists.
jacopone/antigravity-nix is mentioned in this evidence.
The flake provides three packages: the Antigravity 2.0 Base App (default), the Antigravity IDE, and the `agy` CLI, with GUI binaries wrapped in an FHS environment.
By default GUI apps use the system Chrome profile; a `useSystemChromeProfile = false` override omits `--user-data-dir`/`--profile-directory` flags for an isolated profile, working with both variants.
Packages are runnable via `nix run github:jacopone/antigravity-nix` (default), `#google-antigravity-ide`, and `#google-antigravity-cli`, and installable through NixOS, Home Manager, or an overlay.
macOS (darwin) packages evaluate and fetch official builds but are untested; CI verifies Linux only, and GUI apps lack code-signing/quarantine handling so may not launch cleanly.

GUI packages come in two strategies: a default `buildFHSEnv` + bubblewrap sandbox (which sets `no_new_privileges`, blocking sudo/pkexec) and a `no-fhs` variant using `autoPatchelfHook` without sandboxing.

A `srcOverride` package option lets users supply a local tarball when fetchurl fails (CDN unreachable, hash drift), bypassing fetchurl while keeping FHS wrapping, Chrome integration, and desktop entry intact.
Requirements include Nix with flakes, `allowUnfree = true` since Antigravity is proprietary, and Chromium is used automatically on aarch64-linux where Google Chrome is unavailable.
This is an unofficial MIT-licensed packaging of Google's proprietary Antigravity, not affiliated with or endorsed by Google; the CLI is described as successor to the Gemini CLI.
A daily GitHub Actions workflow (07:00 UTC) checks Google Cloud Run endpoints for new versions, verifies hashes, builds, and opens auto-merge PRs; release and branch-cleanup workflows follow.

Repository development practice: contributors fork, create a feature branch, test with `nix build` and `nix flake check`, and submit a PR; CLAUDE.md adds build, version-update, and workflow-testing checklists.
The Antigravity IDE has a known upstream bug on all Linux distributions where it may freeze the system on close; the documented workaround is force-killing the process after closing the window.
